To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ET-1, but not VIC, induces a rapid and transient increase in intracellular calcium-ion concentration and cell contraction in human aortic smooth muscles.

ET-1, a 21-amino acid peptide, is a potent vasocontractor peptide in human vascular smooth muscle and that VIC, a three amino acid different peptide from ET-1 has less activity in increase in intracellular calcium-ion concentration and percent of response cells.
ET-1, but not VIC-LP, induces contraction and calcium-ion increase in cultured human VSM.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ET-1 family and VIC peptides have the ability to contract cultured human VSM and to increase the intracellular calcium-ion concentration, and that the mechanism of action is different from the mechanism of action of VIC-LP, a precursor of VIC.
the cultured human VSM cells are a good system to study the mechanism of signal transduction of ET family peptides and to develop new drugs to treat hypertension and other vascular diseases.
ET-1 and its derivatives have the same mechanism of action in human VSM as they do in other vascular smooth muscle cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ET-1, the most potent vasocontractor peptide, has a rapid action on the cultured human VSM and that VIC-LP is a novel peptide to suppress the action of VIC.
VIC, which is a vasocontractor peptide, has less activity in increasing intracellular calcium-ion concentration than ET-1.
the cultured human VSM may be useful to study the mechanism of the vasocontractor peptide action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human VSM contraction induced by ET-1 and VIC is associated with the transient increase of cytosolic free calcium-ion level.
VIC has a lower potency in the contraction of human vascular smooth muscle than ET-1 and that VIC-like peptide (16 amino acid fragment of precursor protein) suppresses the effect of VIC.
the human vascular endothelial cells are the source of the ET-1, and the ET-1 is a potent vasocontrictor and a mitogenic peptide.
